text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.87% today, continuing a sharp rally that's gained 8.15% over the past two weeks. The immediate driver is escalating Middle East tensions: Iran retaliated against U.S. strikes on Wednesday, and there are reports of mines hitting tankers in the Hormuz Strait—one of the world's critical oil chokepoints through which 17 million barrels transit daily. With Brent crude above $95 and U.S. oil at $91.48, higher crude prices improve refinery margins (the profit refiners make by turning raw oil into gasoline and diesel).

The broader tailwind is U.S. energy policy shifting toward increased oil production: Venezuela is opening new concessions to American operators, and Chevron is investing $7 billion to double production there. These moves signal a tighter global oil market and sustained crude pricing support, which benefits refiners with the capacity to process more barrels. U.S. refineries are already running at 98% capacity, so there's little room to expand operations—but sustained higher oil prices and tight supply conditions typically support refiner profitability.
